material_systems.name: PVA Drywall Primer
material_systems.description: Polyvinyl acetate (PVA) primer for bare drywall walls. Economical, fast-drying, excellent sealing of porous drywall surfaces. Standard choice for new construction production work.

products.notes: PVA-based primers seal porous drywall and provide good holdout for topcoats. Zero stain blocking — sealer only (RC-002). Low VOC, water cleanup.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Latex Primer
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic latex primer for new drywall walls. Superior adhesion, better hide, excellent topcoat holdout. Recommended for QT4 work.

products.notes: Acrylic latex provides better adhesion and build than PVA, and better topcoat compatibility. Zero stain blocking — sealer only (RC-002).

material_systems.name: High-Build Drywall Primer
material_systems.description: High-build primer for Level 5 finish or when maximum wall surface uniformity is required. Fills minor imperfections and creates uniform porosity.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec 500 Interior High Build Primer
products.notes: High-build formula fills minor imperfections and provides uniform porosity across joints and field. May require light sand before topcoat.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Bare drywall wall, proper application thickness, standard porosity. Same absorption characteristics as ceiling drywall.
Level 3 has more exposed paper, higher absorption, lower coverage.
Texture increases surface area, reduces coverage 15-25%.
Premium primer, standard application on smooth drywall wall.
High-build applied at greater thickness, lower coverage by design.

consumables.name: 5-gallon bucket with grid
consumables.notes: Preferred for production work over paint tray.

consumables.name: Spray tip 517
consumables.notes: Standard tip for primer on drywall walls. Same selection as ceilings.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.notes: Reusable floor perimeter protection for roll method. Positioned along base of walls being rolled.

consumables.name: Rosin paper
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for hard floors during wall spray. Taped seams required per Protection_and_Masking_Doctrine.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 1.5 mil
consumables.specification: 1.5 mil plastic sheeting for floor protection
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for carpet during wall spray. Taped edges required per Protection_and_Masking_Doctrine.

consumables.name: Masking tape 1.5-inch

consumables.name: Fine sanding block
consumables.specification: Fine grit sanding block, 150-220 grit range
consumables.notes: For sanding substrate repairs smooth before priming. QT2 does not sand. QT3 spot-sands patches. QT4 sands all repairs thoroughly.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackle
consumables.notes: For filling identified defects during substrate inspection/repair phase. Usage is QT-driven: QT2 minimal, QT3 standard, QT4 comprehensive. New construction = Good condition baseline.

consumable_usage_models.description: Primer material quantity based on wall field area
consumable_usage_models.notes: Select coverage profile based on material system, texture, and drywall finish level. Add 5-10% waste factor for spray methods.

consumable_usage_models.description: Floor protection material for spray/spray_backroll methods
consumable_usage_models.notes: Rosin paper for hard floors, plastic sheeting for carpet. Material selection driven by floor_type site condition. Only included when floor_type is finished or partial (RC-003).

consumable_usage_models.description: Floor protection (perimeter drops) for roll method
consumable_usage_models.formula: Reusable drop cloths positioned along wall perimeter. Count based on room perimeter and drop width.
consumable_usage_models.notes: Canvas drops for roll method. Less material than spray full-floor coverage. Only included when floor_type is finished or partial (RC-003).

consumable_usage_models.description: Tape for floor protection seams (spray methods)
consumable_usage_models.formula: Proportional to floor area — approximately 1 roll per 500 SF of protected floor
consumable_usage_models.notes: Seam tape for rosin paper or plastic sheeting joints. Required per Protection_and_Masking_Doctrine.

consumable_usage_models.description: Roller cover replacement based on wall area
consumable_usage_models.notes: Driven by product count and color count per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine. Nap selected by surface texture. Roller size selected by application method (9" for roll, 18" for spray_backroll).

consumable_usage_models.formula: 1 per material type used (primer = 1 brush minimum)
consumable_usage_models.notes: Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 1 brush per material type. Wall prime uses one material, so 1 brush baseline.
New construction = Good condition (0.5x standard). QT2 uses minimal spackle. QT3/QT4 use based on inspection findings.

compatibility_rules.description: PVA primer is compatible with all latex/acrylic topcoats
compatibility_rules.constraint: Do not use PVA primer under alkyd or oil-based topcoats
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard for NC where finish coats are always latex/acrylic.

compatibility_rules.description: Acrylic latex primer is compatible with all latex, acrylic, and most hybrid topcoats
compatibility_rules.constraint: Verify compatibility with specialty topcoats per PDS

compatibility_rules.description: PVA and acrylic latex primers have zero stain blocking capability (RC-002)
compatibility_rules.constraint: If stain blocking is needed, specify a separate stain blocking product — do not rely on drywall primer
compatibility_rules.notes: Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: PVA/acrylic are sealers, not stain blockers.

risk_notes.description: Level 3 drywall finish has higher absorption and visible joint patterns under primer. Coverage rate drops to ~300 SF/gal. May require discussion with builder about upgrading to Level 4.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use COV_PVA_LEVEL3 profile. Flag to estimator that material cost will be higher.

risk_notes.description: High-build primer may require light sanding before topcoat application. This adds a labor step not present with standard PVA or acrylic primers.
risk_notes.mitigation: SOP Librarian should include conditional sand step when SYS_HIGH_BUILD_PRIMER is selected.

risk_notes.description: Textured walls (orange peel, knockdown) consume 15-25% more primer than smooth walls. Estimators should use textured coverage profiles.
risk_notes.mitigation: Coverage profiles differentiate smooth vs textured. Ensure correct profile is selected.

assumptions.value: Same coverage rates as ceiling prime (identical drywall substrate)
assumptions.note: Drywall absorption is substrate-dependent, not orientation-dependent. Wall and ceiling coverage rates are equivalent.

assumptions.source: Industry standard for airless spray on interior walls
assumptions.note: No doctrine coverage for spray waste factor — derived from industry practice. Wall spray waste may be slightly less than ceiling spray waste because overspray pattern is more directional.

uncertainty_flags.description: Spackle usage in NC is highly variable depending on drywall contractor quality. Good condition NC drywall should need minimal spackle, but field conditions vary.
